places.name: Looshaus
places.note: Loos's 1911 'house without eyebrows', its bare upper facade set against the Hofburg across the square. The scandal that announced modern Vienna.

places.name: Loos American Bar
places.note: A tiny 1908 bar of onyx, marble and mirrors that make it look three times its size. Room for barely twenty; a martini, late.

places.name: Secession
places.note: Olbrich's white temple under a dome of gilded laurel leaves. Klimt's Beethoven Frieze runs round a room in the basement.

places.name: Otto Wagner Pavilion
places.note: Wagner's 1899 metro station pavilions in green iron, marble and gilded sunflowers. Transport as civic jewellery.

places.name: Postsparkasse
places.note: Wagner's savings bank of 1906: granite slabs held on with aluminium bolts, a glass-floored banking hall under a glass roof. Check access before you go.

places.name: MAK
places.note: The Museum of Applied Arts, strong on the Wiener Werkstätte. Bentwood, silver, textiles: the objects behind the architecture.

places.name: Café Prückel
places.note: A 1950s coffee house opposite the MAK: pastel, spacious, unhurried. Newspapers on sticks and a Melange.

places.name: Café Sperl
places.note: An 1880 coffee house with billiard tables and worn velvet, hardly changed since. Sit for hours; no one will move you on.

places.name: Haus Wittgenstein
places.note: The house the philosopher designed for his sister: severe proportions, exact door handles, no ornament at all. Now a Bulgarian cultural institute, seen on guided tours.

places.name: Karl-Marx-Hof
places.note: Red Vienna's monument to social housing, a kilometre of flats with arches big enough for a tram. A small museum in the old laundry tells the story.

places.name: Kirche am Steinhof
places.note: Wagner's church in the grounds of a hospital: white marble skin, a copper and gold dome, windows by Koloman Moser. Limited opening, mostly weekends.

places.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
places.note: Bruegel's room is the reason to come. The domed café under the cupola is the reason to stay.

places.name: Belvedere
places.note: A Baroque palace on a terraced garden, with Klimt's Kiss upstairs. Walk down through the gardens afterwards.

places.name: Leopold Museum
places.note: The world's largest Schiele collection, in a white limestone cube in the MuseumsQuartier.

places.name: Albertina
places.note: A palace of drawings and prints, Dürer's hare among them. Hollein's flying roof blade marks the entrance.

places.name: Wien Museum
places.note: The city museum, reopened with a free permanent collection. Klimt, Loos's living room, and a terrace over Karlsplatz.

places.name: State Hall, National Library
places.note: A Baroque library hall under a frescoed dome, lined with 200,000 books. One of the most beautiful rooms in Europe.

places.name: Zentralfriedhof
places.note: Beethoven, Brahms and Schubert in the musicians' plots, and a Jugendstil church by Max Hegele. Bring time; it's huge.

places.name: Werkbundsiedlung
places.note: A 1932 model estate of small modernist houses by Loos, Rietveld, Neutra and others. A walk through a manifesto.

places.name: Wotruba Church
places.note: A church built from 152 concrete blocks, piled like a sculpture on a hill. Opening hours are limited.

places.name: Majolikahaus
places.note: Wagner's apartment block faced in flowering tiles, beside its gilded neighbour. Best from the Naschmarkt.

places.name: Naschmarkt
places.note: A long market on the river cover, with stalls, cafés and Saturday's flea market. Breakfast, then browse.

places.name: Café Hawelka
places.note: A smoky-brown café of artists and writers, little changed since the 1940s. Buchteln come out of the oven late in the evening.

places.name: Café Bräunerhof
places.note: Thomas Bernhard's café: newspapers, plain marble tables, unhurried waiters. The least touristy of the classics.

places.name: Zum Schwarzen Kameel
places.note: A Jugendstil deli and wine bar, with tiny open sandwiches at the counter. A glass of Grüner Veltliner with them.

places.name: Demel
places.note: The old court confectioner, all mirrors and glass cases of cakes. Watch the pastry chefs through the window.

places.name: Palmenhaus Schönbrunn
places.note: An 1882 iron-and-glass palm house in the palace park, with three climate zones. Visit on a grey winter day.

places.name: Sigmund Freud Museum
places.note: The flat and practice where Freud worked for 47 years. The waiting room remains as it was.

places.name: Musikverein
places.note: The Golden Hall, gilded caryatids and near-perfect acoustics. Hear anything here.

places.name: Wiener Riesenrad
places.note: The 1897 Ferris wheel with its wooden cabins, made famous by The Third Man. Go round once at dusk.

places.name: Augarten Porcelain
places.note: Porcelain made by hand in a Baroque palace in the Augarten park. The shop sells pieces designed by Josef Hoffmann.
